page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System. The server is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 2.5 GHz, delivering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory is configured with 64 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4 GB per virtual core. Hardware acceleration is provided by a dedicated NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU containing 16 GB of VRAM. Networking features a 20 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and storage includes a 225 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume.

Performance benchmarks highlight the instance's strengths in hardware-accelerated tasks, particularly machine learning inference. For small 135M language models, prompt processing reaches 8,447 tokens per second, with text generation at 321 tokens per second. For medium 7B models, prompt processing delivers 1,163 tokens per second alongside 40 tokens per second for generation. In contrast, general-purpose host CPU benchmarks show lower single-core execution metrics, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1,144 and stress-ng score of 1,286. Multi-core metrics sit in the middle tier, with a Passmark CPU score of 14,414 and uncached large-block memory read speeds of 88.11 GB/sec.

By bundling an entry-level enterprise GPU and local NVMe storage with mid-tier host compute, the configuration delivers strong density for inference tasks without the operational footprint of large multi-accelerator nodes. The primary constraint is limited CPU single-thread throughput and the 16 GB VRAM capacity, which bounds model parameters to small and medium architectures. Best-fit deployments include deep learning inference pipelines, video processing, remote workstation rendering, and microservices requiring fast local disk caching alongside GPU acceleration.
